tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: ShareOnboardingGuide
tools.description:
Upload the ONBOARDING.md in the current directory and return a share link teammates can open in Claude Code. Call this after the user has confirmed the final content.

When called with the default mode='check': if a local ONBOARDING.md is present, uploads it to the most-recently-updated org guide (or creates one if none exist) and returns a fresh link. If no local file is present, returns the existing link without uploading (status: has_existing).

'update': upload to a specific guide by short_code. 'create': always make a new link. 'delete': remove a guide.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

input.prompt: How to install the Entire CLI on Windows (scoop, curl script, other), and what `entire enable --agent claude-code` changes in the repo. Also how checkpoints are pushed (entire/checkpoints/v1 branch) and any privacy warnings.

toolu_01YayH4rjeJbfEfoUexSAYx3.prompt: How to install the Entire CLI on Windows (scoop, curl script, other), and what `entire enable --agent claude-code` changes in the repo. Also how checkpoints are pushed (entire/checkpoints/v1 branch) and any privacy warnings.

content.content:
**Windows install**

- **Scoop (stable):** Run `scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git`, then `scoop install entire/entire`. If you have an older install registered as `cli`, the README gives a migration command to run when `entire` is not running.
- **PowerShell script:** Run `irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex`. If Scoop is available, the script uses it for stable releases. Otherwise it verifies the checksum and installs `entire.exe` and `git-remote-entire.exe` to `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`, adding that directory to your user PATH if needed. For nightly builds, use `iex "& {$(irm https://entire.io/install.ps1)} -Channel nightly"`.
- **Go:** Run `go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest`. Also install `git-remote-entire` if you clone over `entire://` URLs. This requires Go 1.27.1 or newer.

The `curl ... install.sh` script is for macOS and Linux, not Windows.

**What `entire enable --agent claude-code` changes**

The README describes these changes:

- It creates Entire settings in `.entire/`. The default `settings.json` contains `"enabled": true` and a `checkpoints` block set to `git-refs`.
- It installs git hooks. If you already have hooks, each one moves to `<hook>.pre-entire`, and Entire's hook runs first, followed by yours.
- It installs Claude Code's hook configuration in `.claude/settings.json`.

Entire does not create commits on your active branch.

**How checkpoints are pushed**

The README does not mention an `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. Checkpoints are stored as individual git refs under `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`, not on a shared branch. Each ref points to a commit containing the checkpoint's metadata, transcripts, and task records. Your commits get an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer that links them to these refs.

By default, checkpoint data is pushed with your normal pushes, but only to one elected remote. Entire chooses it in this order: `checkpoint_push_remote` if set, a remote matching your branch's push destination, `origin`, the only remote if there is exactly one, or the first remote in `.git/config`. You can use a separate repository with `checkpoint_remote`.

**Privacy warnings**

- Session transcripts are stored in your git repository. If the repository is public, anyone can see them.
- Entire redacts detected secrets such as API keys and tokens before writing a checkpoint, but this redaction is best-effort.
- Older Entire versions created `entire/<commit>-<worktree>` shadow branches containing raw snapshots of your working tree. Newer versions don't create them, but leftover branches are not deleted automatically. Run `entire doctor` to find them and `entire doctor --force` to remove them.

content.content:
Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

Existing git hooks are kept: each is moved to <hook>.pre-entire and runs after
Entire's hook.

If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
for you and create an initial commit. It never creates or pushes to a remote —
publish the repository yourself when you're ready.

Usage:
  entire enable [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path               Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                         Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., antigravity, claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.
      --agent-help-skill entire agent-help   Install the stable Entire agent-help skill (points agents at entire agent-help) for selected agent(s)
      --checkpoint-backend string            Checkpoint storage backend: refs (default; one git ref per checkpoint) or branch (legacy shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-push-remote string        Git remote for checkpoint uploads (saved to .entire/settings.local.json, even with --project)
      --checkpoint-remote string             Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format; providers: github, gitlab (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                                Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
  -h, --help                                 help for enable
      --import-history                       During first-time setup, import the selected agents' existing session history (last 30 days) without prompting
      --init-repo                            If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string        Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local                                Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-init-repo                         If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project                              Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --search-skill                         Install the optional Entire search skill for selected agent(s)
      --skip-initial-commit                  Don't create the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --skip-push-sessions                   Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --telemetry                            Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
  -y, --yes                                  Accept all defaults without prompting (in a non-repo directory: init git and commit; then enable all agents and accept telemetry). Does not import existing agent history — see --import-history

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

# NetCortex — Claude Code context (Workstream A, Aun)

## Read first

- **`docs/PARTNER_PLAN.md`** holds the full project context. Read it before any task. Key sections:
  - §2 hackathon rules and partner prizes
  - §3 product
  - §4 end-to-end flow
  - §5 machines and networking
  - §6 who builds what
  - §7 stack, repo layout, conventions
  - §8 shared contracts
  - §10 datasets
  - §11 timeline and gates
  - §13 risks and cut order
- **§9 of that doc is the partner's task list (Workstream B).** Do not build those parts.
- **This file covers Aun's tasks (Workstream A) and the current state of the machines.**
  - If this file and the plan disagree about Workstream A, this file wins.
  - Once `packages/core` is merged, the code is the source of truth for contracts.

**Deadline:** publish the DEV post by **Mon 19 Oct 2026, 10:00 AM Pakistan time** (hard deadline 11:59 AM PKT). Prefer working and simple over complete and clever.

## Current state (keep this section updated)

| Machine | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Laptop (this machine): i7 10th gen, 32 GB RAM, Quadro P520 4 GB | Integration host. All code runs here: Docker, Temporal, CHR, API, workers, collector. | Active. Claude Code in VS Code. |
| Mac mini M4, 16 GB (office machine) | **Model server only.** Ollama with `gemma4:e4b` (agent) and `embeddinggemma` (embeddings). `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`, `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=24h`. **No git, no repo, no code runs there.** | `gemma4:e4b` downloading (about 3 h). Until it's ready, build the agent with Pydantic AI `TestModel`. |
| Partner PC: GTX 1660 6 GB, 16 GB RAM, remote | Workstream B via Codex. Runs his own local Ollama for embeddings, plus Gemma 4 E2B/E4B for development. | Working from `docs/PARTNER_PLAN.md`, against the draft contracts. **Needs `packages/core` merged ASAP.** |

- **Networking:** Tailscale joins the laptop and Mac (Aun's tailnet). The Mac is shared with the partner.
- **Fallback:** if Tailscale fails, pull the partner's code from GitHub and run everything on the laptop. The laptop reaches the Mac over the home LAN.
- **Database:** Tiger Cloud (TimescaleDB + pgvector), shared by both people.

**Do not download large files on the laptop while the Mac model download runs.** Both share the home connection. Small Docker images and the CHR image are fine.

## Folder ownership

**Workstream A (edit freely):**
- `packages/core`, `packages/agent`, `packages/fixes`
- `services/api`, `services/worker`, `services/collector`
- `templates/routeros`
- `infra/` (except `infra/render`)
- `CLAUDE.md`

**Workstream B (do not edit; call their interfaces):**
- `apps/web`
- `packages/detector`, `packages/runbook`, `packages/notify`, `packages/simgen`
- `data/`, `eval/`, `experiments/`
- `.github/workflows`, `infra/render`, `AGENTS.md`

If a partner module is not merged yet, put a stub with the **same interface** in `packages/agent/stubs.py` and switch it out when theirs lands. Never fix a bug in their folders. Write it up for the partner instead.

## Tasks, in order

### A0. Setup (15 min)

- `uv` workspace at the repo root, Python 3.12.
- `ruff` and `pytest` configured.
- `.gitignore`: `.env`, `data/raw`, `data/generated`, `var/`, `.venv`, `node_modules`.
- MIT `LICENSE` if missing.
- Install Entire: `entire enable --agent claude-code`, before the first commit.

### A1. Contracts: `packages/core` (MOST URGENT, the partner is blocked)

1. **`schemas.py`** (pydantic v2): `Cause` and `TemplateId` enums (exact strings from plan §8), `MetricsWindow`, `SeriesForecast`, `DetectionResult`, `RunbookChunk`, `NewsItem`, `NewsCheck`, `ScenarioLabel`, `IncidentReport`, `FixPlan`, `IncidentStatus`.
2. **`settings.py`**: one `Settings` class (pydantic-settings) for every env var in plan §8. Add:
   - `APPLY_TARGET` (`chr` by default; `real` must be set explicitly)
   - `SITE_ID_LIVE` (default `home-lab`)
3. **`interfaces.py`**: `Protocol`s for `detect`, `search_runbook`, `speak`, `check_news`, `inject`, `investigate`, with signatures exactly as in plan §8.
4. **`db.py`**: psycopg 3 connection pool and small helpers to insert metrics and incidents.
5. **`migrations/001_init.sql`**:
   - Enable the extensions `timescaledb` and `vector`.
   - Create all tables from plan §8.
   - Make `probe_metrics`, `iface_metrics` and `forecasts` hypertables.
   - Add indexes on `(site_id, time DESC)`.
6. **Additions beyond the plan** (Aun owns contracts, so add them now and tell the partner):
   - Table `incident_audio(incident_id uuid, lang text, mp3 bytea, created_at timestamptz)` for voice alerts.
   - Table `events(id bigserial, time, kind text, payload jsonb)`, plus a `NOTIFY netcortex_events` trigger. The API's SSE stream reads from it.
   - Seed a `home-lab` site for the live collector.
7. **`.env.example`** with every variable, and these values filled in:
   - `AGENT_MODEL=gemma4:e4b`
   - `EMBED_MODEL=embeddinggemma`
   - `OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://<mac-tailscale-name>:11434`

**Done when:**
- `uv run pytest packages/core` passes.
- The migration applies cleanly to Tiger Cloud.
- The code is merged to `main`.
- A short message to the partner lists the merged interfaces and the additions in step 6.

### A2. Infra

- **`infra/docker-compose.yml`:**
  - Temporal dev server (or document `temporal server start-dev` if the CLI is simpler).
  - Optional local TimescaleDB with pgvector for offline work.
- **`infra/scripts/check_ollama.py`:** confirms the Mac is reachable, both models are listed, and an embedding has 768 dimensions.

**Done when:** Temporal UI opens on the laptop and `check_ollama.py` passes. Until the model finishes downloading, it is allowed to report "agent model missing".

### A3. Live collector: `services/collector`

- An async loop using `icmplib`.
- **Pings, every 10 s, for each target:**
  - Targets: gateway (home router), upstream hop (find it with a traceroute at startup, then fix it), `1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8`, one regional game server (configurable).
  - Send a burst of 5 pings per target.
  - Latency = average RTT; jitter = standard deviation of the RTTs; loss = % of pings lost.
- **Router stats, every 30 s:** read interface and queue stats from the RouterOS REST API (CHR now, a real MikroTik if one is available). If no router is configured, collect pings only.
- Writes rows with `source = live` and `site_id = SITE_ID_LIVE`.
- Survives errors: log, skip the round, keep running.
- One command starts it: `uv run collector`.

**Done when:** it runs unattended for an hour and rows keep appearing. **Start it as early as possible.** The partner's calibration needs hours of real data.

### A4. Virtual router: `infra/chr`

- **`start.sh`:**
  - Downloads the CHR x86 image (free license, 1 Mbps cap is fine).
  - Boots it in QEMU and forwards the REST API (HTTP) and SSH ports to localhost.
  - Waits until the REST API answers.
- **`reset.sh`:** restores a clean snapshot.
- **`baseline.rsc`:** baseline config:
  - `ether1` = primary uplink, `ether2` = backup uplink, `ether3` = LAN
  - A couple of simple queues
  - A DNS config
- **`test_templates.py`:** for every template, applies it with valid sample params, checks the result with `/export`, rolls back, and checks the config matches baseline. Exits non-zero on failure. **The partner's GitHub Actions workflow runs this script.**

### A5. Fix templates: `templates/routeros/*.yaml`

Four files: `queue_limit`, `failover_route`, `priority_queue`, `dns_servers`. Each has:
- `id`
- `description` (one plain sentence)
- `allowed_causes`
- `params` (each with a type plus range, regex or enum)
- `apply` (Jinja template of RouterOS commands)
- `rollback` (Jinja template)
- `verify` (which series should improve, and by how much)

`none` is a built-in with no commands.

Check every command against RouterOS v7 syntax. If unsure, test it on CHR before committing.

### A6. Fix checker: `packages/fixes`

1. `validate(template_id, params)`: rejects any value outside the schema.
2. `render(template_id, params)`: returns `(commands, rollback)`.
3. `dry_run(template_id, params)`, on CHR:
   - export the config before
   - apply
   - export the config after and diff it
   - roll back
   - export again and confirm it matches the original
4. Store the result in `fix_plans`.
5. `apply(...)`: used after human approval. It targets CHR unless `APPLY_TARGET=real`.

Talk to CHR through the REST API; SSH (`asyncssh`) is the fallback if a command can't run via REST. **Never touch a real router unless `APPLY_TARGET=real` is set explicitly.**

### A7. Agent: `packages/agent`

- **Model:** a Pydantic AI `Agent` using an OpenAI-compatible provider at `OLLAMA_BASE_URL/v1`, model `AGENT_MODEL`. Output type: `IncidentReport`.
- **Tools:**
  - `get_metrics(series, minutes)`
  - `get_forecast(series)`
  - `search_runbook(query)` (partner)
  - `check_news(provider, target)` (partner)
  - `list_templates(cause)`: returns only the templates allowed for that cause, plus `none`
- **Instructions to the model:**
  - Pick `template_id` only from `list_templates`.
  - Params must fit the schema.
  - Never write raw commands.
  - Say "unsure" with low confidence rather than guessing.
  - Customer messages must be short, in English and Urdu.
- **`investigate(site_id, detection, window) -> IncidentReport`**, async. If the model's output fails validation, retry once with the validation error fed back to the model. If it fails again, fall back to `template_id = none`.
- **Until `gemma4:e4b` finishes downloading:** develop and test with Pydantic AI `TestModel` / `FunctionModel`. Add one live smoke test marked `@pytest.mark.live`.

### A8. Workflows: `services/worker` (Temporal)

**`MonitorSiteWorkflow`**, one per site:
- Every 60 s, an activity:
  - loads the last 30 minutes plus history
  - calls `detect()` and writes forecasts
  - opens an incident if `is_anomaly` is true and no open incident exists for that site and cause
  - starts `IncidentWorkflow`
- Uses continue-as-new periodically.

**`IncidentWorkflow`:**
1. Investigate with Pydantic AI's `TemporalAgent` wrapper.
2. Run the fix check (`dry_run`).
3. Call `speak()` for EN and UR and store the audio in `incident_audio`. This is optional: if it fails, continue.
4. Set the status to `awaiting_approval` and wait for an `approve` or `reject` signal, up to 2 h.
5. If approved: `apply()`, wait 5 minutes, verify.

1. `validate(template_id, params)`: rejects any value outside the schema.
2. `render(template_id, params)`: returns `(commands, rollback)`.
3. `dry_run(template_id, params)`, on CHR:
   - export the config before
   - apply
   - export the config after and diff it
   - roll back
   - export again and confirm it matches the original
4. Store the result in `fix_plans`.
5. `apply(...)`: used after human approval. It targets CHR unless `APPLY_TARGET=real`.

Talk to CHR through the REST API; SSH (`asyncssh`) is the fallback if a command can't run via REST. **Never touch a real router unless `APPLY_TARGET=real` is set explicitly.**

  - `get_forecast(series)`
  - `search_runbook(query)` (partner)
  - `check_news(provider, target)` (partner)
  - `list_templates(cause)`: returns only the templates allowed for that cause, plus `none`

  - Pick `template_id` only from `list_templates`.
  - Params must fit the schema.
  - Never write raw commands.
  - Say "unsure" with low confidence rather than guessing.
  - Customer messages must be short, in English and Urdu.

**`MonitorSiteWorkflow`**, one per site:
- Every 60 s, an activity:
  - loads the last 30 minutes plus history
  - calls `detect()` and writes forecasts
  - opens an incident if `is_anomaly` is true and no open incident exists for that site and cause
  - starts `IncidentWorkflow`
- Uses continue-as-new periodically.

**`IncidentWorkflow`:**
1. Investigate with Pydantic AI's `TemporalAgent` wrapper.
2. Run the fix check (`dry_run`).
3. Call `speak()` for EN and UR and store the audio in `incident_audio`. This is optional: if it fails, continue.
4. Set the status to `awaiting_approval` and wait for an `approve` or `reject` signal, up to 2 h.
5. If approved: `apply()`, wait 5 minutes, verify.
6. If the key metric improved, mark `resolved`. If not, run rollback and mark `rolled_back`. If rejected or timed out, mark `rejected`.

"""Shared data contracts. Every package imports these; nobody redefines them.

Times are timezone-aware UTC everywhere. The UI converts to Pakistan time.
"""

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Any, Literal
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import pandas as pd
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator

EMBED_DIM = 768  # EmbeddingGemma vector size; runbook_chunks.embedding is vector(768)


# --- Vocabulary -------------------------------------------------------------


class Cause(StrEnum):
    UPLINK_CONGESTION = "uplink_congestion"
    HEAVY_USER = "heavy_user"
    UPSTREAM_DEGRADATION = "upstream_degradation"
    GAME_ROUTE_ISSUE = "game_route_issue"
    WIRELESS_INTERFERENCE = "wireless_interference"
    UPLINK_DOWN = "uplink_down"
    DNS_SLOW = "dns_slow"
    NORMAL = "normal"


class TemplateId(StrEnum):
    QUEUE_LIMIT = "queue_limit"  # limit one IP or subnet
    FAILOVER_ROUTE = "failover_route"  # backup default route with check-gateway=ping
    PRIORITY_QUEUE = "priority_queue"  # prioritise gaming and DNS traffic
    DNS_SERVERS = "dns_servers"  # switch DNS resolvers
    NONE = "none"  # no config fix; notify only


class IncidentStatus(StrEnum):
    OPEN = "open"
    AWAITING_APPROVAL = "awaiting_approval"
    APPLYING = "applying"
    VERIFYING = "verifying"
    RESOLVED = "resolved"
    ROLLED_BACK = "rolled_back"
    REJECTED = "rejected"


CLOSED_STATUSES = frozenset(
    {IncidentStatus.RESOLVED, IncidentStatus.ROLLED_BACK, IncidentStatus.REJECTED}
)


class Source(StrEnum):
    LIVE = "live"  # the live collector
    SIM = "sim"  # simulator: generate, replay or inject
    RIPE = "ripe"  # RIPE Atlas public measurements


class ProbeKind(StrEnum):
    ICMP = "icmp"  # rtt_ms is the ping round trip
    DNS = "dns"  # rtt_ms is the DNS lookup time; target key is "dns:<resolver>"


class TargetRole(StrEnum):
    GATEWAY = "gateway"
    UPSTREAM_HOP = "upstream_hop"
    PUBLIC_DNS = "public_dns"
    GAME_SERVER = "game_server"


class UplinkRole(StrEnum):
    PRIMARY = "primary"
    BACKUP = "backup"
    BACKHAUL = "backhaul"


class EventKind(StrEnum):
    """`events.kind`, also the SSE `event:` name on /stream."""

    METRIC = "metric"
    INCIDENT_OPENED = "incident.opened"
    INCIDENT_UPDATED = "incident.updated"
    FIX_TESTED = "fix.tested"
    FIX_APPLIED = "fix.applied"


# --- Series keys ------------------------------------------------------------

SeriesKind = Literal["probe", "iface", "subscriber"]


def series_key(kind: SeriesKind, name: str, metric: str) -> str:
    """Build a key like `probe:8.8.8.8:rtt_ms`, `probe:dns:1.1.1.1:rtt_ms`, `iface:ether1:util_pct`."""
    return f"{kind}:{name}:{metric}"


def parse_series_key(key: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    """Split a series key into (kind, name, metric). The name may contain colons."""
    kind, rest = key.split(":", 1)
    name, metric = rest.rsplit(":", 1)
    if kind not in ("probe", "iface", "subscriber") or not name or not metric:
        raise ValueError(f"not a series key: {key!r}")
    return kind, name, metric


# --- Sites ------------------------------------------------------------------


class Uplink(BaseModel):
    iface: str
    role: UplinkRole
    capacity_mbps: float | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)
    gateway: str | None = None  # next-hop IP; needed by failover_route


class ProbeTarget(BaseModel):
    key: str  # value of probe_metrics.target, e.g. "8.8.8.8" or "dns:1.1.1.1"
    host: str  # what is pinged or queried
    kind: ProbeKind = ProbeKind.ICMP
    role: TargetRole


class Site(BaseModel):
    """Row of `sites`; `uplinks` and `targets` are the jsonb columns."""

    id: str
    name: str
    uplinks: list[Uplink] = []
    targets: list[ProbeTarget] = []
    subscribers: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)


# --- Metric rows ------------------------------------------------------------


class ProbeMetric(BaseModel):
    time: datetime
    site_id: str
    target: str
    kind: ProbeKind = ProbeKind.ICMP
    rtt_ms: float | None = Field(ge=0)  # response time: ICMP round trip or DNS lookup time
    jitter_ms: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    loss_pct: float = Field(ge=0, le=100)
    source: Source


class IfaceMetric(BaseModel):
    time: datetime
    site_id: str
    iface: str
    rx_bps: int = Field(ge=0)
    tx_bps: int = Field(ge=0)
    util_pct: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    drops: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)
    errors: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)
    source: Source


class SubscriberMetric(BaseModel):
    """Per-subscriber traffic (e.g. from RouterOS simple-queue counters); needed for heavy_user."""

    time: datetime
    site_id: str
    ip: str
    rx_bps: int = Field(ge=0)
    tx_bps: int = Field(ge=0)
    source: Source


PROBE_COLUMNS = tuple(ProbeMetric.model_fields)
IFACE_COLUMNS = tuple(IfaceMetric.model_fields)
SUBSCRIBER_COLUMNS = tuple(SubscriberMetric.model_fields)


def _empty_frame(columns: tuple[str, ...]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return pd.DataFrame(columns=list(columns))


class MetricsWindow(BaseModel):
    """A slice of metrics for one site: DataFrames with the columns of the tables above.

    Rows have `time` <= `as_of`. Extra columns are allowed; missing ones are an error.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)

    as_of: datetime
    probe_metrics: pd.DataFrame = Field(default_factory=lambda: _empty_frame(PROBE_COLUMNS))
    iface_metrics: pd.DataFrame = Field(default_factory=lambda: _empty_frame(IFACE_COLUMNS))
    subscriber_metrics: pd.DataFrame = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: _empty_frame(SUBSCRIBER_COLUMNS)
    )

    @field_validator("as_of")
    @classmethod
    def _utc(cls, value: datetime) -> datetime:
        if value.tzinfo is None:
            raise ValueError("as_of must be timezone-aware")
        return value.astimezone(UTC)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _has_columns(self) -> MetricsWindow:
        for name, columns in (
            ("probe_metrics", PROBE_COLUMNS),
            ("iface_metrics", IFACE_COLUMNS),
            ("subscriber_metrics", SUBSCRIBER_COLUMNS),
        ):
            missing = set(columns) - set(getattr(self, name).columns)
            if missing:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} is missing columns: {sorted(missing)}")
        return self


# --- Detector ---------------------------------------------------------------


class ForecastPoint(BaseModel):
    time: datetime  # the future time being forecast
    p10: float
    p50: float
    p90: float

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _ordered(self) -> ForecastPoint:
        if not self.p10 <= self.p50 <= self.p90:
            raise ValueError("forecast quantiles must satisfy p10 <= p50 <= p90")
        return self


class SeriesForecast(BaseModel):
    series_key: str  # see series_key()
    points: list[ForecastPoint]  # horizons 1..5 minutes ahead


class DetectionResult(BaseModel):
    is_anomaly: bool
    score: float = Field(ge=0, le=1)  # anomaly score
    series: list[SeriesForecast] = []
    cause_guess: Cause
    cause_confidence: float = Field(ge=0, le=1)
    evidence: list[str] = []  # short sentences, e.g. "uplink ether1 at 97% for 6 min"
    model: str  # e.g. "tabpfn-3.5"; stored in forecasts.model
    mode: Literal["cloud", "local", "mock"]


# --- Docs search and side services ------------------------------------------


class RunbookChunk(BaseModel):
    title: str
    section: str | None = None
    text: str
    source_url: str
    score: float  # higher is more relevant (e.g. 1 - cosine distance)


class NewsItem(BaseModel):
    title: str
    url: str
    published: datetime | None = None


class NewsCheck(BaseModel):
    """Result of the "is it us or them?" check.

    `available=False` means the check could not run (no key, timeout, bad response). It is
    never the same as "no outage reported"; `summary` says why.
    """

    available: bool = True
    outage_reported: bool = False
    summary: str
    items: list[NewsItem] = []


# --- Simulator --------------------------------------------------------------


class ScenarioLabel(BaseModel):
    id: UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid4)
    site_id: str
    scenario_type: Cause
    start_at: datetime
    end_at: datetime | None = None
    affected: dict[str, Any] = {}  # e.g. {"iface": "ether1"} or {"ip": "10.0.0.42"}
    expected_cause: Cause
    expected_template: TemplateId
    expected_params: dict[str, Any] = {}
    seed: int | None = None
    source: Source = Source.SIM


# --- Agent output -----------------------------------------------------------


class IncidentReport(BaseModel):
    """What the agent returns. Validated before anything else sees it."""

    summary: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=500)  # 1-2 plain English sentences
    likely_cause: Cause
    confidence: float = Field(ge=0, le=1)
    evidence: list[str] = []
    upstream_check: NewsCheck | None = None
    template_id: TemplateId
    template_params: dict[str, Any] = {}  # checked against the template schema by fixes
    customer_message_en: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=320)
    customer_message_ur: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=320)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _none_has_no_params(self) -> IncidentReport:
        if self.template_id is TemplateId.NONE and self.template_params:
            raise ValueError("template 'none' takes no params")
        return self


# --- Incidents and fixes ----------------------------------------------------


class FixPlan(BaseModel):
    id: UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid4)
    incident_id: UUID
    template_id: TemplateId
    params: dict[str, Any] = {}
    commands: str = ""  # rendered from the template, never written by the model
    rollback: str = ""
    dry_run_ok: bool | None = None  # None until the CHR dry run has finished
    dry_run_log: str = ""
    decision: Literal["approved", "rejected"] | None = None
    decided_by: str | None = None
    decided_at: datetime | None = None


class Incident(BaseModel):
    id: UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid4)
    site_id: str
    opened_at: datetime
    closed_at: datetime | None = None
    status: IncidentStatus = IncidentStatus.OPEN
    cause: Cause
    confidence: float = Field(ge=0, le=1)
    detection: DetectionResult | None = None
    report: IncidentReport | None = None
    source: Source


class Event(BaseModel):
    """Row of `events`; the API streams these over SSE (`id:` = id, `event:` = kind)."""

    id: int | None = None
    time: datetime
    kind: EventKind
    payload: dict[str, Any] = {}

"""One Settings class for every environment variable.

Field names are the lowercase env var names (DATABASE_URL -> database_url). Secrets are
SecretStr, so they never show up in logs, reprs or tracebacks; call .get_secret_value()
at the point of use. NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables are read by apps/web only.
"""

from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import AliasChoices, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    # Shared database (Tiger Cloud: TimescaleDB + pgvector)
    database_url: SecretStr | None = None

    # Models (Ollama on the Mac, OpenAI-compatible API at <base>/v1)
    ollama_base_url: str = "http://localhost:11434"
    agent_model: str = "gemma4:e4b"
    embed_model: str = "embeddinggemma"  # must be identical on both sides, or search breaks

    # Detector
    tabpfn_mode: Literal["cloud", "local"] = "cloud"
    tabpfn_token: SecretStr | None = Field(
        default=None, validation_alias=AliasChoices("TABPFN_TOKEN", "TABPFN_API_KEY")
    )

    # Optional cloud add-ons; missing keys make them unavailable, never blocking
    elevenlabs_api_key: SecretStr | None = None
    elevenlabs_voice_id: str | None = None
    serpapi_api_key: SecretStr | None = None
    sentry_dsn_backend: str | None = None

    # Runtime
    temporal_address: str = "localhost:7233"
    demo_mode: bool = False
    http_timeout_s: float = Field(default=10.0, gt=0)  # default for every outbound call

    # Routers. Fixes go to CHR unless APPLY_TARGET=real is set explicitly.

"""Signatures of the module functions the workflows and the agent call.

Failure rules (the same for every module):
- detect() and search_runbook() raise ModuleUnavailable when their model, provider or data
  can't produce a real answer. An empty list from search_runbook() means "no matches".
- speak() returns b"" when voice is unavailable.
- check_news() returns NewsCheck(available=False, summary=<reason>) when it can't check.
- Every network call inside a module has a finite timeout (Settings.http_timeout_s by default).
Callers treat any of these as "skip this step"; an unavailable module never blocks an incident.
"""

import inspect
from typing import Literal, Protocol

from netcortex_core.schemas import (
    Cause,
    DetectionResult,
    IncidentReport,
    MetricsWindow,
    NewsCheck,
    RunbookChunk,
    ScenarioLabel,
)


class ModuleUnavailable(RuntimeError):
    """A module could not produce a real result. Subclass it (e.g. DetectorUnavailable)."""


class Detect(Protocol):  # packages/detector
    def __call__(
        self, site_id: str, window: MetricsWindow, history: MetricsWindow
    ) -> DetectionResult: ...


class SearchRunbook(Protocol):  # packages/runbook
    def __call__(self, query: str, k: int = 5) -> list[RunbookChunk]: ...


class Speak(Protocol):  # packages/notify; returns MP3 bytes
    def __call__(self, text: str, lang: Literal["en", "ur"]) -> bytes: ...


class CheckNews(Protocol):  # packages/notify
    def __call__(self, provider: str | None, target: str | None) -> NewsCheck: ...


class Inject(Protocol):  # packages/simgen
    def __call__(
        self, site_id: str, scenario_type: Cause, duration_min: int, seed: int | None
    ) -> ScenarioLabel: ...


class Investigate(Protocol):  # packages/agent
    async def __call__(
        self, site_id: str, detection: DetectionResult, window: MetricsWindow
    ) -> IncidentReport: ...


def conforms(func: object, protocol: type) -> bool:
    """True if `func` takes the same parameters (names, order, defaults) as the protocol.

    Use it in tests: `assert conforms(detect, Detect)`.
    """
    expected = list(inspect.signature(protocol.__call__).parameters.values())[1:]  # drop self
    actual = list(inspect.signature(func).parameters.values())  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    if [(p.name, p.kind, p.default) for p in actual] != [
        (p.name, p.kind, p.default) for p in expected
    ]:
        return False
    return inspect.iscoroutinefunction(func) == inspect.iscoroutinefunction(protocol.__call__)

-- NetCortex initial schema. Every statement is idempotent, so re-running is safe.
-- All times are timestamptz (UTC).

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;

-- Sites ----------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sites (
    id          text PRIMARY KEY,
    name        text NOT NULL,
    uplinks     jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',   -- [{iface, role, capacity_mbps, gateway}]
    targets     jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',   -- [{key, host, kind, role}]
    subscribers int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Metrics (hypertables) --------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS probe_metrics (
    time      timestamptz NOT NULL,
    site_id   text NOT NULL,
    target    text NOT NULL,                  -- "8.8.8.8", or "dns:1.1.1.1" for DNS lookups
    kind      text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'icmp' CHECK (kind IN ('icmp', 'dns')),
    rtt_ms    double precision,               -- NULL when every probe was lost
    jitter_ms double precision,
    loss_pct  double precision NOT NULL CHECK (loss_pct BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
    source    text NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('live', 'sim', 'ripe'))
);
COMMENT ON COLUMN probe_metrics.rtt_ms IS
    'response time in ms: ICMP round trip, or DNS lookup time when kind = dns';
SELECT create_hypertable('probe_metrics', by_range('time'), if_not_exists => TRUE);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS probe_metrics_site_time ON probe_metrics (site_id, time DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS iface_metrics (
    time     timestamptz NOT NULL,
    site_id  text NOT NULL,
    iface    text NOT NULL,
    rx_bps   bigint NOT NULL,
    tx_bps   bigint NOT NULL,
    util_pct double precision,                -- NULL when capacity is unknown
    drops    bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    errors   bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    source   text NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('live', 'sim', 'ripe'))
);
SELECT create_hypertable('iface_metrics', by_range('time'), if_not_exists => TRUE);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS iface_metrics_site_time ON iface_metrics (site_id, time DESC);

-- Per-subscriber traffic, so heavy_user can name the offending IP.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS subscriber_metrics (
    time    timestamptz NOT NULL,
    site_id text NOT NULL,
    ip      text NOT NULL,
    rx_bps  bigint NOT NULL,
    tx_bps  bigint NOT NULL,
    source  text NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('live', 'sim', 'ripe'))
);
SELECT create_hypertable('subscriber_metrics', by_range('time'), if_not_exists => TRUE);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS subscriber_metrics_site_time ON subscriber_metrics (site_id, time DESC);

-- Written only by the monitor workflow; re-running a detection overwrites the same row.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS forecasts (
    time       timestamptz NOT NULL,          -- the future time being forecast
    site_id    text NOT NULL,
    series_key text NOT NULL,                 -- probe:<target>:rtt_ms, iface:<iface>:util_pct, ...
    p10        double precision NOT NULL,
    p50        double precision NOT NULL,
    p90        double precision NOT NULL,
    model      text NOT NULL
);
SELECT create_hypertable('forecasts', by_range('time'), if_not_exists => TRUE);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS forecasts_site_time ON forecasts (site_id, time DESC);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS forecasts_key ON forecasts (site_id, series_key, model, time);

-- Incidents and fixes ------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS incidents (
    id         uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    site_id    text NOT NULL,
    opened_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    closed_at  timestamptz,
    status     text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN (
                   'open', 'awaiting_approval', 'applying', 'verifying',
                   'resolved', 'rolled_back', 'rejected')),
    cause      text NOT NULL CHECK (cause IN (
                   'uplink_congestion', 'heavy_user', 'upstream_degradation', 'game_route_issue',
                   'wireless_interference', 'uplink_down', 'dns_slow', 'normal')),
    confidence double precision,
    detection  jsonb,                         -- DetectionResult
    report     jsonb,                         -- IncidentReport
    source     text NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('live', 'sim', 'ripe'))
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS incidents_site_time ON incidents (site_id, opened_at DESC);
-- At most one open incident per site and cause.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS incidents_one_open ON incidents (site_id, cause)
    WHERE closed_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fix_plans (
    id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    incident_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES incidents (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    template_id text NOT NULL CHECK (template_id IN (
                    'queue_limit', 'failover_route', 'priority_queue', 'dns_servers', 'none')),
    params      jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    commands    text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    rollback    text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    dry_run_ok  boolean,
    dry_run_log text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    decision    text CHECK (decision IN ('approved', 'rejected')),
    decided_by  text,
    decided_at  timestamptz,
    created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS fix_plans_incident ON fix_plans (incident_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS incident_audio (
    incident_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES incidents (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    lang        text NOT NULL CHECK (lang IN ('en', 'ur')),
    mp3         bytea NOT NULL,
    created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (incident_id, lang)
);

-- Simulator labels ---------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scenario_labels (
    id                uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    site_id           text NOT NULL,
    scenario_type     text NOT NULL,
    start_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    end_at            timestamptz,
    affected          jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    expected_cause    text NOT NULL,
    expected_template text NOT NULL,
    expected_params   jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    seed              int,
    source            text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'sim'
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS scenario_labels_site_time ON scenario_labels (site_id, start_at DESC);

-- Docs search ------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS runbook_chunks (
    id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    source_url  text NOT NULL,
    title       text NOT NULL,
    section     text,
    text        text NOT NULL,
    embedding   vector(768),
    embed_model text NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS runbook_chunks_embedding
    ON runbook_chunks USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- Events for the UI's SSE stream -------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    id      bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
    time    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    kind    text NOT NULL,                    -- incident.opened, incident.updated, fix.tested, ...
    payload jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_time ON events (time DESC);

-- NOTIFY carries only id and kind (payloads can exceed NOTIFY's 8 kB limit);
-- the API reads the row by id.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION notify_netcortex_event() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    PERFORM pg_notify('netcortex_events',
                      json_build_object('id', NEW.id, 'kind', NEW.kind)::text);
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS events_notify ON events;
CREATE TRIGGER events_notify AFTER INSERT ON events

"""Database access: one psycopg 3 connection pool and small insert helpers.

Helpers take an open connection so the caller decides the transaction:

    with get_pool().connection() as conn:
        insert_probe_metrics(conn, rows)
"""

from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID

from psycopg import Connection
from psycopg.types.json import Jsonb
from psycopg_pool import ConnectionPool
from pydantic import BaseModel

from netcortex_core.schemas import (
    CLOSED_STATUSES,
    IFACE_COLUMNS,
    PROBE_COLUMNS,
    SUBSCRIBER_COLUMNS,
    DetectionResult,
    EventKind,
    IfaceMetric,
    Incident,
    IncidentStatus,
    ProbeMetric,
    Site,
    SubscriberMetric,
)
from netcortex_core.settings import Settings, get_settings

CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S = 10

_pool: ConnectionPool | None = None


def database_url(settings: Settings | None = None) -> str:
    settings = settings or get_settings()
    if settings.database_url is None:
        raise RuntimeError("DATABASE_URL is not set (see .env.example)")
    return settings.database_url.get_secret_value()


def get_pool(settings: Settings | None = None) -> ConnectionPool:
    """The process-wide pool, created on first use."""
    global _pool
    if _pool is None:
        _pool = ConnectionPool(
            database_url(settings),
            min_size=1,
            max_size=5,
            timeout=CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S,
            kwargs={"connect_timeout": CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S},
            open=True,
        )
    return _pool


def close_pool() -> None:
    global _pool
    if _pool is not None:
        _pool.close()
        _pool = None


def _value(value: Any) -> Any:
    """Python value -> what psycopg should send. Enums go as their string value."""
    if isinstance(value, Enum):
        return value.value
    if isinstance(value, BaseModel):
        return Jsonb(value.model_dump(mode="json"))
    if isinstance(value, dict | list):
        return Jsonb(value)
    return value


def _insert_many(
    conn: Connection, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], rows: Iterable[BaseModel]
) -> int:
    values = [tuple(_value(getattr(row, c)) for c in columns) for row in rows]
    if not values:
        return 0
    placeholders = ", ".join(["%s"] * len(columns))
    sql = f"INSERT INTO {table} ({', '.join(columns)}) VALUES ({placeholders})"
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.executemany(sql, values)
    return len(values)


def insert_probe_metrics(conn: Connection, rows: Iterable[ProbeMetric]) -> int:
    return _insert_many(conn, "probe_metrics", PROBE_COLUMNS, rows)


def insert_iface_metrics(conn: Connection, rows: Iterable[IfaceMetric]) -> int:
    return _insert_many(conn, "iface_metrics", IFACE_COLUMNS, rows)


def insert_subscriber_metrics(conn: Connection, rows: Iterable[SubscriberMetric]) -> int:
    return _insert_many(conn, "subscriber_metrics", SUBSCRIBER_COLUMNS, rows)


def upsert_forecasts(conn: Connection, site_id: str, detection: DetectionResult) -> int:
    """Write the detector's forecast bands. Re-running a detection overwrites the same rows."""
    values = [
        (point.time, site_id, series.series_key, point.p10, point.p50, point.p90, detection.model)
        for series in detection.series
        for point in series.points
    ]
    if not values:
        return 0
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO forecasts (time, site_id, series_key, p10, p50, p90, model) "
            "VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s) "
            "ON CONFLICT (site_id, series_key, model, time) "
            "DO UPDATE SET p10 = EXCLUDED.p10, p50 = EXCLUDED.p50, p90 = EXCLUDED.p90",
            values,
        )
    return len(values)


def upsert_site(conn: Connection, site: Site) -> None:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "INSERT INTO sites (id, name, uplinks, targets, subscribers) "
            "VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s) "
            "ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, uplinks = EXCLUDED.uplinks, "
            "targets = EXCLUDED.targets, subscribers = EXCLUDED.subscribers",
            (
                site.id,
                site.name,
                Jsonb([u.model_dump(mode="json") for u in site.uplinks]),
                Jsonb([t.model_dump(mode="json") for t in site.targets]),
                site.subscribers,
            ),
        )


def insert_incident(conn: Connection, incident: Incident) -> UUID:
    """Insert a new incident. Fails (unique index) if one is already open for site + cause."""
    columns = ("id", "site_id", "opened_at", "closed_at", "status", "cause", "confidence",
               "detection", "report", "source")  # fmt: skip
    _insert_many(conn, "incidents", columns, [incident])
    return incident.id


def set_incident_status(conn: Connection, incident_id: UUID, status: IncidentStatus) -> None:
    """Change status; closing statuses also set closed_at."""
    closed = status in CLOSED_STATUSES
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "UPDATE incidents SET status = %s, "
            "closed_at = CASE WHEN %s THEN now() ELSE closed_at END WHERE id = %s",
            (status.value, closed, incident_id),
        )


def insert_event(conn: Connection, kind: EventKind, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
    """Append to `events`; the table's trigger NOTIFYs the API's SSE stream."""
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "INSERT INTO events (kind, payload) VALUES (%s, %s) RETURNING id",
            (kind.value, Jsonb(payload)),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    assert row is not None
    return row[0]

from netcortex_core.settings import get_settings


class _Conn(Protocol):
    def execute(self, query: str, params: tuple = ..., /) -> psycopg.Cursor: ...
    def transaction(self) -> psycopg.Transaction: ...


def migrations() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(version, sql) for every bundled migration, in order. Version = file name without .sql."""
    folder = files("netcortex_core") / "migrations"
    paths = sorted((p for p in folder.iterdir() if p.name.endswith(".sql")), key=lambda p: p.name)
    return [(p.name.removesuffix(".sql"), p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) for p in paths]


def apply_pending(conn: _Conn) -> list[str]:
    """Apply migrations not yet recorded; return the versions applied now."""
    conn.execute(
        "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations ("
        "version text PRIMARY KEY, applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())"
    )
    applied = {row[0] for row in conn.execute("SELECT version FROM schema_migrations").fetchall()}
    done = []
    for version, sql in migrations():
        if version in applied:
            continue
        with conn.transaction():
            conn.execute(sql)
            conn.execute("INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES (%s)", (version,))
        done.append(version)
    return done


def scrub(text: str, url: str) -> str:
    """Remove the URL and its password from an error message."""
    secrets = [url]
    try:
        password = conninfo_to_dict(url).get("password")
    except psycopg.ProgrammingError:
        password = None
    if password:
        secrets.append(str(password))
    for secret in secrets:
        text = text.replace(secret, "***")
    return text


def main() -> int:
    settings = get_settings()
    if settings.database_url is None:
        print("DATABASE_URL is not set. Put it in .env (see .env.example).", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    url = settings.database_url.get_secret_value()
    try:
        with psycopg.connect(url, connect_timeout=CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S, autocommit=True) as conn:
            done = apply_pending(conn)
    except Exception as exc:  # report any failure without leaking the URL
        print(f"Migration failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {scrub(str(exc), url)}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"Applied: {', '.join(done)}" if done else "Database is up to date.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""`uv run netcortex-migrate`: apply pending SQL migrations to DATABASE_URL.

Safe to re-run: applied versions are recorded in schema_migrations and skipped, and each
migration file is itself idempotent. Never prints the database URL or its password.
"""

import sys
from importlib.resources import files

import psycopg
from psycopg.conninfo import conninfo_to_dict

from netcortex_core.db import CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S
from netcortex_core.settings import get_settings


def migrations() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(version, sql) for every bundled migration, in order. Version = file name without .sql."""
    folder = files("netcortex_core") / "migrations"
    paths = sorted((p for p in folder.iterdir() if p.name.endswith(".sql")), key=lambda p: p.name)
    return [(p.name.removesuffix(".sql"), p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) for p in paths]


def apply_pending(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> list[str]:
    """Apply migrations not yet recorded; return the versions applied now."""
    conn.execute(
        "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations ("
        "version text PRIMARY KEY, applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())"
    )
    applied = {row[0] for row in conn.execute("SELECT version FROM schema_migrations").fetchall()}
    done = []
    for version, sql in migrations():
        if version in applied:
            continue
        with conn.transaction():
            conn.execute(sql)
            conn.execute("INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES (%s)", (version,))
        done.append(version)
    return done

    """Remove the URL and its password from an error message."""
    secrets = [url]
    try:

    except psycopg.ProgrammingError:
        password = None
    if password:
        secrets.append(str(password))
    for secret in secrets:
        text = text.replace(secret, "***")
    return text

# netcortex-core

Shared contracts for every NetCortex package. Import from here; never redefine these types.

```python
from netcortex_core import Cause, DetectionResult, MetricsWindow, Settings, get_settings
```

| Module | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `schemas.py` | `Cause`, `TemplateId`, `IncidentStatus`, metric rows, `MetricsWindow`, `DetectionResult`, `RunbookChunk`, `NewsCheck`, `ScenarioLabel`, `IncidentReport`, `FixPlan`, `Incident`, `Event`, `Site`, series-key helpers |
| `settings.py` | `Settings`: one field per env var, lowercase (`DATABASE_URL` -> `database_url`). Secrets are `SecretStr`. |
| `interfaces.py` | `Protocol`s for `detect`, `search_runbook`, `speak`, `check_news`, `inject`, `investigate`; `ModuleUnavailable`; `conforms()` for tests |
| `db.py` | psycopg 3 pool (`get_pool()`) and insert helpers for metrics, forecasts, incidents and events |
| `migrations/` | SQL migrations, applied by `netcortex-migrate` |

## Conventions

- Times are timezone-aware UTC. `MetricsWindow` rejects naive `as_of`.
- `probe_metrics.rtt_ms` is the response time: ICMP round trip, or DNS lookup time when
  `kind = 'dns'`. DNS targets use keys like `dns:1.1.1.1`. `rtt_ms` is NULL on total loss.
- Series keys: `probe:<target>:<metric>`, `iface:<iface>:<metric>`, `subscriber:<ip>:<metric>`.
  Use `series_key()` / `parse_series_key()`; target names may contain colons.
- Failure rules for modules are in the `interfaces.py` docstring.

## Database

```bash
uv run netcortex-migrate          # apply pending migrations to DATABASE_URL (safe to re-run)
uv run netcortex-migrate --list   # list bundled migrations, no connection
```

It reads `DATABASE_URL` through `Settings` (from `.env`) and never prints it.

## Tests

```bash
uv run pytest packages/core
```

Unit tests only, with no network and no `.env`.

## feat(core): shared contracts, root workspace and migrations (A0 + A1)

This PR adds `packages/core` (import `netcortex_core`, distribution `netcortex-core`) and the root workspace files. Once it merges, **the code here is the source of truth for every shared type**, replacing plan §8.

### Root files

- `.gitignore`, `LICENSE` and `.gitattributes` are taken from `b/workstream-b`, with these changes:
  - `.gitignore` adds `var/`, `*credentials*.env` and `.claude/settings.local.json`.
  - `.gitignore` no longer ignores `.entire/`, so `.entire/settings.json` is committed. Entire's own `.entire/.gitignore` keeps the local files out.
- `pyproject.toml` is based on his version, with these changes:
  - **Python 3.14** (`requires-python = ">=3.14,<3.15"`, plus `.python-version`).
  - Workspace members are globs (`packages/*`, `services/*`), so the file works before and after the Workstream B packages land.
  - `netcortex-core` is a root dependency, so a plain `uv sync` installs it.
  - The `live` pytest marker is registered. His config uses `--strict-markers`.
  - `testpaths` are globs (`packages/*/tests`, `services/*/tests`, `infra/*/tests`, `.github/tests`), so missing folders don't break a run.
  - His ruff config is unchanged except `target-version = "py314"`.
- `uv.lock` is regenerated on this branch.
- `.claude/settings.json` holds Entire's hooks plus a rule that stops Claude Code from reading `.env`. The repo and its Entire transcripts are public.

### Contracts in this PR

**Vocabulary** (`schemas.py`, exact strings from plan §8):
- `Cause`, `TemplateId`, `IncidentStatus`
- `Source` (`live|sim|ripe`), `ProbeKind` (`icmp|dns`), `TargetRole`, `UplinkRole`
- `EventKind` (`metric`, `incident.opened`, `incident.updated`, `fix.tested`, `fix.applied`)

**Schemas** (pydantic v2):

| Type | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `ProbeMetric` | `time, site_id, target, kind, rtt_ms, jitter_ms, loss_pct, source` |
| `IfaceMetric` | `time, site_id, iface, rx_bps, tx_bps, util_pct, drops, errors, source` |
| `SubscriberMetric` | `time, site_id, ip, rx_bps, tx_bps, source` |
| `MetricsWindow` | `as_of` (aware, normalised to UTC), `probe_metrics`, `iface_metrics`, `subscriber_metrics`. These are DataFrames with at least the columns above; extras are allowed. |
| `ForecastPoint` / `SeriesForecast` | `time, p10 <= p50 <= p90` / `series_key, points` (horizons +1..+5 min) |
| `DetectionResult` | `is_anomaly, score (0..1), series, cause_guess, cause_confidence, evidence, model, mode ("cloud"/"local"/"mock")` |
| `RunbookChunk` | `title, section, text, source_url, score` (higher = more relevant) |
| `NewsItem` / `NewsCheck` | `title, url, published` / `available, outage_reported, summary, items` |
| `ScenarioLabel` | `id, site_id, scenario_type, start_at, end_at, affected, expected_cause, expected_template, expected_params, seed, source` |
| `IncidentReport` | the plan's fields. `summary` is at most 500 chars and each customer message at most 320; template `none` must have empty params. |
| `FixPlan`, `Incident`, `Event`, `Site`, `Uplink`, `ProbeTarget` | DB row shapes |

Helpers in `schemas.py`:
- `series_key()` / `parse_series_key()`, for keys like `probe:dns:1.1.1.1:rtt_ms`.
- `PROBE_COLUMNS`, `IFACE_COLUMNS`, `SUBSCRIBER_COLUMNS`.
- `EMBED_DIM = 768`.

**Settings** (`settings.py`): one `Settings` class whose field names are the env var names in lowercase.

| Field | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `database_url` | SecretStr, unset |
| `ollama_base_url` | `http://localhost:11434` |
| `agent_model` | `gemma4:e4b` |
| `embed_model` | `embeddinggemma` |
| `tabpfn_mode` | `cloud` (or `local`) |
| `tabpfn_token` | SecretStr; reads `TABPFN_TOKEN` or `TABPFN_API_KEY` |
| `elevenlabs_api_key`, `serpapi_api_key` | SecretStr |
| `elevenlabs_voice_id`, `sentry_dsn_backend` | unset |
| `temporal_address` | `localhost:7233` |
| `demo_mode` | `false` |
| `http_timeout_s` | `10` |
| `apply_target` | `chr` (`real` must be set explicitly) |
| `chr_rest_url`, `chr_username`, `chr_password` | `chr_username` is `admin` |
| `site_id_live` | `home-lab` |

- Empty env values count as unset.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables are in `.env.example` but belong to `apps/web` only.
- Use `get_settings()` for the cached instance.

**Interfaces** (`interfaces.py`): `Protocol`s with the plan §8 signatures:
- `Detect`, `SearchRunbook`, `Speak`, `CheckNews`, `Inject`, `Investigate` (async).
- `ModuleUnavailable`, which modules subclass (for example `DetectorUnavailable`).
- `conforms(func, Protocol)` for tests.

**Failure rules**, the same for every module:
- `detect()` and `search_runbook()` raise `ModuleUnavailable` when they can't produce a real answer. An empty list from `search_runbook()` means "no matches".
- `speak()` returns `b""` when voice is unavailable.
- `check_news()` returns `NewsCheck(available=False, summary=<reason>)` when it can't check.

1. `subscriber_metrics` hypertable and `MetricsWindow.subscriber_metrics`, so `heavy_user` can name an IP.
